proposal.hypothesis: The parent’s row-column-K order walks B with a stride of n and performs no parallel work. Tiled i-k-j accumulation makes B and C accesses contiguous in the output-column loop; keeping an 8x128 C tile and 32x128 B panel active should improve locality. Static ownership of disjoint 8-row tiles can use up to eight threads for larger matrices, while serial execution below n=256 avoids parallel overhead on small cases. These are unmeasured expectations, not a speedup claim.

retained: Zero the complete output on every call, then compute generic positive n dimensions without packing or explicit intrinsics.
Tile the row, output-column, and K loops (8x128x32) while keeping the inner output-column loop contiguous and processing K blocks in ascending order.
Use static OpenMP scheduling over disjoint row tiles for n >= 256, clamp worker count to 1..8, and use a serial path for smaller cases.
